rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only baseline is already competitive before adding image data, multiprofile aggregation, or multimodal fusion. config_001 tests the minimal RNA-only single-profile PCA model, providing a low-cost validation accuracy/F1 reference for later comparisons of RNA encoders, profile settings, and multimodal designs. It is the best first experiment under a limited budget because it isolates a core baseline without changing multiple design choices and avoids assuming that more complex multimodal models will automatically perform better.

Only config_001 is known: RNA-only PCA with a single profile has moderate validation accuracy and F1, so the effect of using multiple profiles is still unknown. config_002 keeps the model setting and RNA encoder fixed while adding multiprofile with the simplest aggregation option, avgpool, directly testing whether profile aggregation improves over the single-profile baseline. This is a minimal, informative extension before changing RNA representation, image modality, or fusion, making it the most efficient use of the next limited budget.

config_002 shows that multiprofile PCA with avgpool improves substantially over singleprofile PCA, suggesting multiprofile RNA aggregation is a promising direction. config_003 changes only the aggregation method from avgpool to transformer, directly testing whether a more expressive profile aggregator improves validation accuracy/F1 or whether avgpool is already sufficient. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest current evidence while isolating the effect of aggregation before moving to new encoders, image modalities, or fusion.

Existing evidence shows that for PCA RNA, multiprofile with avgpool is much stronger than singleprofile and also stronger than transformer aggregation, with both accuracy and F1 supporting this. The major remaining uncertainty is whether the image modality provides useful signal at all, and whether the same profile/aggregation setting transfers to image features. config_011 tests an image-only ResNet-50 baseline under the currently promising multiprofile/avgpool setting, changing mainly the modality relative to config_002. This gives a necessary unimodal image baseline before testing fusion, helping isolate whether image features are informative rather than confounding image usefulness with fusion strategy or RNA encoder choice.

The strongest result so far is RNA-only multiprofile with PCA and avgpool (config_002: 0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), showing that multiprofile aggregation is more useful than singleprofile or transformer aggregation for the current PCA representation. Image-only ResNet is weak, so the next clean extension is to test RNA representation within the best unimodal setting. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder from PCA to scvi_n200 while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, isolating whether a learned nonlinear RNA representation improves on PCA. This is high-information under a limited budget: if it helps, it identifies a better RNA encoder for later multimodal tests; if not, PCA remains the preferred RNA representation.

The strongest result so far is RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and avgpool, while PCA multiprofile showed avgpool outperforming transformer. This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation can improve on the current best scvi/avgpool setup by changing only aggregation. It is the best next step because it exploits the most promising RNA-only direction and clarifies whether more complex profile aggregation is worthwhile before adding image or fusion complexity.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only scvi_n200 multiprofile is the strongest unimodal direction (0.650 avgpool, 0.653 transformer), and multiprofile helped pca_n2000 versus singleprofile, but scvi singleprofile is untested. config_004 directly tests whether the profile/aggregation gain is general to the best RNA encoder by changing only profile setting relative to config_005/006. This is the best next use of budget because it isolates an important design choice, avoids assuming multiprofile is necessary, and will determine whether later multimodal tests should use a simpler singleprofile or keep multiprofile aggregation.

RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile is the strongest tested direction (config_005/006, ~0.65 accuracy and ~0.63 F1), while image-only ResNet50 is weak (config_011, ~0.33 accuracy). The key uncertainty is whether adding image information to the best RNA representation provides complementary signal. config_030 keeps the RNA side identical to the strong config_005 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) and adds only ResNet50 with simple concat fusion, matching the already tested image-only ResNet50 setting. This isolates the effect of multimodal fusion rather than changing aggregation or image encoder, making it the most informative next experiment under a limited budget.

RNA-only scvi multiprofile is currently the strongest direction (0.650-0.653 accuracy), while the only multimodal test (scvi + resnet50, avgpool, concat) is slightly below RNA-only at 0.632 and image-only resnet50 is weak at 0.328. The main unresolved question is whether the multimodal underperformance is due to naive concatenation fusion. config_031 changes only fusion from concat to weighted relative to config_030, directly testing whether adaptive fusion can allow the image modality to help without changing the already informative RNA encoder, profile, or aggregation. This is a minimal, high-value comparison for deciding whether multimodal fusion is worth further exploration.

The strongest evidence is that scvi_n200 with multiprofile RNA features is promising, and multimodal weighted fusion with resnet50 and avgpool (config_031) is currently the best result at 0.6776 validation accuracy. The main remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation improves this best multimodal setup, since RNA-only transformer aggregation was only marginally better than avgpool. config_033 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping scvi_n200, multiprofile, resnet50, and weighted fusion, so it isolates the aggregation effect. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest promising direction with a minimal one-variable extension, potentially improving performance while clearly learning whether aggregation matters in the top-performing multimodal setting.
